claims.text: Mechanical deformation continuously exposes fresh reactive surface sites during simultaneous wear and corrosion.
Freshly exposed reactive sites trigger rapid formation of a self-healing passivating oxide layer.
Reactive alloying elements such as Cr, Al, or Ti regenerate the passivating oxide film.
The regenerated oxide film acts as a dynamic barrier to mechanical wear.
The regenerated oxide film acts as a dynamic barrier to chemical corrosion.
The target high-entropy alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
The target alloy contains reactive elements prone to forming stable oxides.
Mechanical abrasion creates new alloy surfaces that rapidly oxidize.
Formation of the protective film reduces overall material loss.
Cyclic removal and reformation of the oxide film produces a beneficial wear-corrosion synergy that enhances durability.
Under combined wear and corrosion, the alloy will have lower overall material loss than in isolated-wear or isolated-corrosion baseline tests.
A continuously regenerating protective film will be observable under combined wear and corrosion.
In the isolated-wear or isolated-corrosion baselines, a protective film either will not form or will regenerate too slowly.
Similar alloys with lower reactive-element enrichment have higher material-loss rates because a protective oxide film is absent or forms more slowly.
The predicted protection holds when abrasion promotes film renewal without exceeding the kinetics of film formation.
The protection may fail when abrasive forces remove the film faster than it can reform.
The protection may fail when the corrosive medium chemically disrupts the film faster than it forms.

contradictions.description: The comparator is not defined consistently. The predicted outcome compares combined degradation with isolated wear or isolated corrosion, the baseline additionally changes reactive-element enrichment, and the falsification experiment compares two compositions both under simultaneous wear-corrosion. These are different controls and cannot be treated as one matched baseline.

The conditions field says wear-only and corrosion-only tests isolate synergistic effects, whereas the baseline field also changes alloy chemistry. Changing both exposure mode and composition prevents that baseline from isolating synergy.
